=== build.yml ===
name: Build APK

# Why CI instead of a local build:
#
# The sandbox this fork was developed in has 2 cores and 2 GB of RAM, so a
# build takes 31-33 minutes and the Kotlin compiler has to be forced
# in-process to avoid the OOM killer. Worse, the toolchain is wiped between
# sessions, so every attempt re-downloads the JDK, the SDK and a 3 GB NDK.
#
# A GitHub runner has 4 cores and 16 GB, caches Gradle between runs, and the
# result is reproducible by anyone. ubuntu-latest specifically: Eden's native
# build is CMake + NDK and is developed against Linux; windows-latest would
# add path-length and line-ending failures for no benefit.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      build_type:
        description: "debug keeps every symbol; release runs R8 and compresses the dex"
        type: choice
        options: [debug, release]
        default: debug
      upload_to_gofile:
        description: "Also upload the APK to gofile.io"
        type: boolean
        default: true
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'patch/**'
      - '.github/workflows/build.yml'

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90

    steps:
      - name: Check out this fork
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          path: fork

      - name: Check out upstream Eden
        run: |
          # depth 50 rather than 1: git apply --3way needs history to resolve
          # a context mismatch instead of failing outright.
          #
          # Retried, and with a mirror behind it. git.eden-emu.dev answered 502
          # mid-build once and took the whole run down with it - every later
          # step skipped, thirty minutes lost, and nothing wrong with the code.
          # sj0404-collab/eden-upstream-reference is our own untouched copy of
          # the same v0.2.1 tree, kept for exactly this.
          ok=0
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if git clone --branch v0.2.1 \
                 https://git.eden-emu.dev/eden-emu/eden.git eden 2>/tmp/clone.log; then
              ok=1; break
            fi
            echo "attempt $attempt failed:"; tail -3 /tmp/clone.log
            rm -rf eden
            sleep $((attempt * 10))
          done

          if [ "$ok" != 1 ]; then
            # AT THE TAG. Cloning the mirror's default branch pulls a
            # different commit, and the build then dies in CMake with an error
            # that looks like ours. That cost two runs on build2.yml.
            echo "::warning::upstream is unreachable; falling back to our mirror at v0.2.1"
            git clone --branch v0.2.1 \
              https://github.com/sj0404-collab/eden-upstream-reference.git eden \
              || { echo "::error::neither upstream nor the mirror could be cloned"; exit 1; }
          fi

          cd eden
          rev=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
          echo "upstream: $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
          expected=58c1e20ee58efa3900ba616207d460886214480b
          if [ "$rev" != "$expected" ]; then
            echo "::error::wrong upstream commit: $rev (expected v0.2.1)"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "  ok   upstream is v0.2.1"

      - name: Set up JDK 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Set up Android SDK
        uses: android-actions/setup-android@v3

      - name: Install NDK, CMake and glslang
        run: |
          sdkmanager --install "ndk;28.2.13676358" "cmake;3.31.6" "build-tools;35.0.0" "platforms;android-36"
          sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y glslang-tools

      - name: Cache Gradle
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.gradle/caches
            ~/.gradle/wrapper
          key: gradle-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('fork/patch/**') }}
          restore-keys: gradle-${{ runner.os }}-

      # ── Кэш объектов C++ ────────────────────────────────────────────
      #
      # 1353 объекта пересобираются каждый раз, а патч трогает Kotlin.
      # Замерено на build2.yml: 25 минут -> 2-3 минуты, попаданий 99.94%.
      #
      # Путь ДОЛЖЕН совпадать с CCACHE_DIR ниже: в первой попытке кэш
      # сохранялся в ~/.ccache, а ccache писал в ~/.cache/ccache, и вся
      # затея молча не работала.
      - name: Cache the C++ objects
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/ccache
          # НЕ github.run_number. Номер прогона каждый раз новый, значит
          # сборка #47 клала кэш под именем -47, а #48 искала -48 и не
          # находила: "Cache not found for input keys", 0.86% попаданий и
          # тридцать минут компиляции с нуля. Запасной поиск по префиксу
          # спасал только когда предыдущая сборка успевала дойти до шага
          # сохранения - а падавшие не доходили, и так три раза подряд.
          #
          # Ключ теперь зависит от того, что реально влияет на объекты C++:
          # версии апстрима и содержимого патча, который трогает .cpp. Тот
          # же код - тот же ключ - прямое попадание.
          key: ccache-symbiosis-v0.2.1-${{ inputs.build_type || 'debug' }}-${{ hashFiles('fork/patch/upstream_changes.patch', 'fork/patch/native_symbiosis.cpp') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ccache-symbiosis-v0.2.1-${{ inputs.build_type || 'debug' }}-
            ccache-symbiosis-v0.2.1-
            ccache-symbiosis-

      - name: Set up ccache
        run: |
          sudo apt-get install -y -qq ccache > /dev/null
          echo "CCACHE_DIR=$HOME/.cache/ccache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          export CCACHE_DIR="$HOME/.cache/ccache"
          mkdir -p "$CCACHE_DIR"
          ccache --set-config=max_size=3G
          # Абсолютные пути и mtime компилятора на новом раннере каждый раз
          # другие - без этих трёх настроек не совпадало даже то, что
          # только что собрали.
          ccache --set-config=base_dir="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          ccache --set-config=hash_dir=false
          ccache --set-config=compiler_check=content
          ccache --zero-stats
          ccache --show-config | grep -E "max_size|cache_dir|base_dir"

      - name: Apply the Symbiosis patch
        run: |
          cd eden
          bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/apply_patch.sh" \
            --patch "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/patch" --eden "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/eden"

      - name: Check for duplicate resources
        # aapt2 only reports this ~20 minutes into the build, after the whole
        # native core has compiled, and does not say which file is at fault.
        # A duplicate that upstream already defines is the usual cause.
        run: python3 fork/tools/check_resources.py eden/src/android/app/src/main/res

      - name: Check JNI names match on both sides
        run: |
          # JNI binds by name at runtime: a mismatch compiles, links, ships and
          # then throws UnsatisfiedLinkError the first time the feature is
          # used. The mangling trap is that an underscore already in a name
          # becomes _1, so yuzu_emu must be written yuzu_1emu - the easiest
          # possible typo, and invisible until it crashes.
          python3 fork/tools/check_jni_names.py --patch fork/patch

      - name: Check Kotlin references resolve
        run: |
          # A missing import only surfaces at compileLegacyDebugKotlin, which
          # is twenty-three minutes into the build - after the entire native
          # tree has compiled. That cost one full run for KenjiProbeService.
          python3 fork/tools/check_kotlin_refs.py --patch fork/patch

      - name: Check string references resolve
        # aapt2 reports a missing @string only at resource-link time, roughly
        # twenty minutes into the build. This is the same check in a second.
        run: python3 fork/tools/check_string_refs.py eden/src/android/app/src/main/res

      - name: Run host tests
        # These gate the build deliberately: each was written after a bug
        # reached the user, and each fails against the code that shipped it.
        run: |
          # Ubuntu 24.04 packages fmt 9, but Eden's logging.h calls
          # format.get(), added in fmt 10. Build against the version Eden
          # expects rather than the distribution one.
          git clone --depth 1 --branch 10.2.1 https://github.com/fmtlib/fmt.git /tmp/fmt
          export FMT_INCLUDE=/tmp/fmt/include
          curl -sL -o /tmp/kc.zip https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin/releases/download/v2.0.21/kotlin-compiler-2.0.21.zip
          unzip -q /tmp/kc.zip -d /tmp
          export PATH="/tmp/kotlinc/bin:$PATH"
          bash fork/tools/run_tests.sh --eden "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/eden" --max-skip 3

      - name: Check the Russian localisation
        run: |
          cd eden/src/android/app/src/main/res
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET, re, sys
          def load(p):
              return {e.get('name'): ''.join(e.itertext())
                      for e in ET.parse(p).getroot().iter('string')}
          en, ru = load('values/strings.xml'), load('values-ru/strings.xml')
          fmt = lambda s: sorted(re.findall(r'%(\d+\$[sd]|[sd%])', s))
          bad = [k for k in ru if k in en and fmt(en[k]) != fmt(ru[k])]
          if bad:
              print('format-argument mismatch:', bad[:5]); sys.exit(1)
          print(f'EN {len(en)} / RU {len(ru)} strings, format arguments agree')
          PY

      - name: Build
        run: |
          cd eden/src/android
          # No --no-daemon: the daemon is what lets Gradle keep the Kotlin
          # compiler warm, and the runner has the memory for it. Also ask
          # CMake for every core - the native compile is the long pole and
          # was previously limited to one worker.
          # Release is what the 25 MB budget refers to. Measured on the debug
          # APK: classes.dex and classes15.dex are 22 MB and are STORED
          # UNCOMPRESSED - the same bytes deflate to 9.2 MB, and R8 removes a
          # good deal more before that. Debug stays the default because it
          # keeps the symbols that make a crash report readable.
          TYPE="${{ inputs.build_type }}"
          TYPE="${TYPE:-debug}"
          # Апстрим уже читает YUZU_ANDROID_ARGS для доп. флагов CMake, так
          # что ccache подключается без правки его build-файлов. Переменные
          # окружения тут НЕ работают: AGP сам вызывает CMake и не передаёт
          # их в этап конфигурации.
          CCACHE_FLAGS="-DCMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache"
          if [ "$TYPE" = "release" ]; then
            ./gradlew assembleLegacyRelease -PYUZU_ANDROID_ARGS="$CCACHE_FLAGS" \
              --parallel --build-cache --max-workers="$(nproc)"
          else
            ./gradlew assembleLegacyDebug -PYUZU_ANDROID_ARGS="$CCACHE_FLAGS" \
              --parallel --build-cache --max-workers="$(nproc)"
          fi

      - name: How much the cache saved
        if: always()
        run: ccache --show-stats | head -12

      - name: Verify the fixes actually shipped
        # objdump and dex strings, not a green tick: a build can succeed with
        # a Kotlin file that was never copied into place.
        run: |
          APK=$(find eden -name "*legacy-release.apk" -o -name "*legacy-debug.apk" | head -1)
          echo "APK: $APK ($(du -h "$APK" | cut -f1))"
          echo "MD5: $(md5sum "$APK" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
          mkdir -p /tmp/x && cd /tmp/x && unzip -qo "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$APK" 'classes*.dex' 'lib/*/*.so' 2>/dev/null || \
            unzip -qo "$APK" 'classes*.dex' 'lib/*/*.so'
          fail=0

          # R8 renames Kotlin methods in a release build, so looking for
          # restoreGameDirs there proves nothing and would fail a perfectly
          # good APK. Native symbols survive either way - they are the JNI
          # contract and cannot be renamed - so those are checked always, and
          # the Kotlin names only when they are meant to be present.
          case "$APK" in
            *release*) MINIFIED=1 ;;
            *)         MINIFIED=0 ;;
          esac

          if [ "$MINIFIED" = 0 ]; then
            for sym in restoreGameDirs rememberGameDirs hasActionableButton; do
              if strings classes*.dex | grep -q "$sym"; then echo "  ok   $sym in dex"
              else echo "  MISSING $sym"; fail=1; fi
            done
          else
            echo "  (release build: Kotlin names are minified, skipping that check)"
          fi

          NM=$(find "$ANDROID_HOME/ndk" -name llvm-nm | head -1)
          n=$("$NM" -D lib/arm64-v8a/libyuzu-android.so | grep -c NativeSymbiosis || true)
          echo "  JNI symbols exported: $n"
          [ "$n" -ge 50 ] || { echo "  too few JNI symbols"; fail=1; }

          # The Kenji bridge, in both names. The core dlopen()s libkenjinxjni
          # and calls debug_break from inside deviceInitialize, so a missing
          # copy is a crash on the first device call rather than a warning.
          for lib in libsymbiosis_kenji.so libkenjinxjni.so; do
            if [ -f "lib/arm64-v8a/$lib" ]; then echo "  ok   $lib present"
            else echo "  MISSING $lib"; fail=1; fi
          done
          for sym in debug_break setRenderingThread setCurrentTransform; do
            if "$NM" -D lib/arm64-v8a/libkenjinxjni.so | grep -q " $sym$"; then
              echo "  ok   $sym exported for the core"
            else echo "  MISSING $sym in libkenjinxjni.so"; fail=1; fi
          done

          # What the 25 MB budget is actually about.
          python3 - "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$APK" <<'SIZEPY' | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import sys, zipfile, os
          apk = sys.argv[1]
          z = zipfile.ZipFile(apk)
          total = os.path.getsize(apk)
          dex = sum(i.compress_size for i in z.infolist() if i.filename.endswith('.dex'))
          dex_raw = sum(i.file_size for i in z.infolist() if i.filename.endswith('.dex'))
          so = sum(i.compress_size for i in z.infolist() if i.filename.endswith('.so'))
          stored = sum(i.file_size for i in z.infolist() if i.compress_type == 0)
          mb = lambda b: b / 1048576
          print("## APK size")
          print()
          print("| | |")
          print("|---|---|")
          print(f"| APK | **{mb(total):.1f} MB** |")
          print(f"| dex | {mb(dex):.1f} MB packed (from {mb(dex_raw):.1f} MB) |")
          print(f"| native libraries | {mb(so):.1f} MB packed |")
          print(f"| stored uncompressed | {mb(stored):.1f} MB |")
          print()
          print(("Under the 25 MB target." if mb(total) <= 25
                 else f"Over the 25 MB target by {mb(total) - 25:.1f} MB."))
          SIZEPY

          exit $fail

      - name: Upload the APK as an artefact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: Eden-Symbiosis-Legacy-debug
          path: eden/src/android/app/build/outputs/apk/**/*.apk
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Upload to gofile.io
        # Default to uploading. inputs.* is empty for a push-triggered run, so
        # the plain condition silently skipped the step and the summary carried
        # no download link - the APK existed only as an artifact, which needs a
        # signed-in browser and expires. Only an explicit false opts out.
        if: github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' || inputs.upload_to_gofile
        run: |
          APK=$(find eden -name "*legacy-release.apk" -o -name "*legacy-debug.apk" | head -1)
          SRV=$(curl -s https://api.gofile.io/servers | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['servers'][0]['name'])")
          curl -s -F "file=@$APK" "https://$SRV.gofile.io/contents/uploadfile" -o /tmp/up.json
          python3 - <<'PY' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import json
          d = json.load(open('/tmp/up.json'))['data']
          print(f"## APK\n\n- **Download:** {d['downloadPage']}\n- **MD5:** `{d['md5']}`\n- **Size:** {round(d['size']/1048576,1)} MB")
          PY
          cat "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

=== build2.yml ===
name: Build clean

# Builds official Eden with patch2 on top - four modified files, nothing else.
#
# WHY A SECOND WORKFLOW
#   build.yml applies the old Symbiosis tree: 13 extra screens, 376 KB of C++,
#   and the retro launcher whose early return in SetWindowAdaptPass() caused
#   the settings crash. This one starts from clean upstream and adds only what
#   was actually asked for, so anything that breaks here is mine and recent.
#
# WHAT PATCH2 CHANGES
#   Game.kt          a game records the folder it was found in
#   GameHelper.kt    that folder is carried down the scan; depth 3 -> 24
#   GamesFragment.kt the list is ordered by folder, then by title
#   GameAdapter.kt   that folder is shown on the card
#   SharedDataDirectory.kt   the shared-folder utility, unchanged
#
# THE CORE STAYS INSIDE THE APK
#   Splitting it out into a folder was tried and abandoned: it cost four
#   failed installs and never once produced a working build. The core is
#   loaded by Eden's own untouched System.loadLibrary, exactly as upstream
#   does it. patch2 no longer contains NativeLibrary.kt at all - there is
#   nothing left in it to change.
#
#   Nothing is created, moved or written. Folder permissions stay read-only and
#   config.ini is untouched.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      build_type:
        description: "debug keeps symbols; release runs R8"
        type: choice
        options: [debug, release]
        default: debug
      upload_to_gofile:
        description: "Also upload the APK to gofile.io"
        type: boolean
        default: true
      apply_patch:
        description: "off = plain upstream Eden, no patch at all (control build)"
        type: boolean
        default: true
      patch_subset:
        description: "which parts of patch2 to apply: all | folders | button | shared"
        type: choice
        options: [all, ui, status, folders, depth3, scan, sort, button, shared, minimal]
        default: all
      flavour:
        description: "mainline (upstream default) or legacy (what the working control was built with)"
        type: choice
        options: [mainline, legacy]
        default: mainline
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'patch2/**'
      - 'tools/apply_patch2.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/build2.yml'

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90

    steps:
      - name: Check out this fork
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          path: fork

      - name: Check out upstream Eden
        run: |
          # Retried, with our mirror behind it: git.eden-emu.dev answered 502
          # mid-build once and took the whole run down with it.
          ok=0
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if git clone --branch v0.2.1 \
                 https://git.eden-emu.dev/eden-emu/eden.git eden 2>/tmp/clone.log; then
              ok=1; break
            fi
            echo "attempt $attempt failed:"; tail -3 /tmp/clone.log
            rm -rf eden
            sleep $((attempt * 10))
          done
          if [ "$ok" != 1 ]; then
            # The mirror, AT THE TAG. This fallback used to clone the mirror's
            # default branch, which is a different commit entirely - so when
            # upstream answered 502 the build silently switched to other code
            # and died in CMake with an error that looked like ours. Twice.
            echo "::warning::upstream unreachable; using our mirror at v0.2.1"
            git clone --branch v0.2.1 \
              https://github.com/sj0404-collab/eden-upstream-reference.git eden \
              || { echo "::error::neither upstream nor the mirror could be cloned"; exit 1; }
          fi

          cd eden
          rev=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
          echo "upstream: $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"

          # Whichever source answered, it must be the tag we build against.
          # Anything else is a different emulator wearing the same directory
          # name, and the failure surfaces 20 minutes later as a C++ error.
          expected=58c1e20ee58efa3900ba616207d460886214480b
          if [ "$rev" != "$expected" ]; then
            echo "::error::wrong upstream commit: $rev (expected v0.2.1 = $expected)"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "  ok   upstream is v0.2.1"

      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - uses: android-actions/setup-android@v3

      - name: Install NDK, CMake and glslang
        run: |
          sdkmanager --install "ndk;28.2.13676358" "cmake;3.31.6" \
            "build-tools;35.0.0" "platforms;android-36" > /dev/null
          sudo apt-get update -qq
          sudo apt-get install -y -qq glslang-tools > /dev/null

      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.gradle/caches
            ~/.gradle/wrapper
          key: gradle2-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('eden/src/android/**/*.gradle*') }}
          restore-keys: gradle2-${{ runner.os }}-

      # ── Why the build took twenty-five minutes ──────────────────────
      #
      # Measured from a real run's timestamps:
      #     12:49:41  Kotlin compiled
      #     12:51:38  ninja started
      #     13:11:56  APK ready          <- twenty minutes of C++
      #
      # 1353 C++ objects were rebuilt from scratch. patch2 contains nine .kt
      # files and three .xml files and NOT ONE .cpp - so every second of that
      # was spent recompiling code nobody touched.
      #
      # ccache fixes exactly this: identical source plus identical flags means
      # the object file is copied out of the cache instead of compiled. The
      # first run after this fills the cache and is no faster; every run after
      # that skips the part that dominates the clock.
      # ── Two bugs in the first attempt at this, both proved by run #9 ──
      #
      # BUG 1: THE CACHE WAS SAVED SOMEWHERE ELSE THAN IT WAS READ
      #   The path here said ~/.ccache. ccache itself reported
      #       (default) cache_dir = /home/runner/.cache/ccache
      #   so 1678 freshly compiled objects were written to a directory the
      #   cache action never packed. Nothing was wrong with ccache and nothing
      #   was wrong with the key - the two halves simply pointed at different
      #   folders. CCACHE_DIR is now set explicitly and the path below is the
      #   same variable, so they cannot drift apart again.
      #
      # BUG 2: HASHED PATHS DEFEAT THE CACHE ACROSS RUNS
      #   NDK builds bake absolute paths into the object; ccache's default
      #   direct mode hashes the compiler binary's mtime too. On a fresh
      #   runner that is a different value every time, which is why run #9
      #   showed 0.89% hits even for the objects it had just built - the 15
      #   hits it did get were all "preprocessed", never "direct".
      #   base_dir + hash_dir=false + compiler_check=content fix exactly that.
      - name: Cache the C++ objects
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          # Must match CCACHE_DIR below. It did not, and that alone cost the
          # entire 20 minutes this step exists to save.
          path: ~/.cache/ccache
          # Keyed on the upstream tag, not on our patch: our patch never
          # changes a .cpp, so a new key would throw away a cache that is
          # still perfectly valid.
          # Не github.run_number: он новый на каждом запуске, поэтому
          # прямого попадания не бывает никогда - только запасной поиск по
          # префиксу, а он не срабатывает, если прошлая сборка упала до
          # шага сохранения. patch2 не трогает ни одного .cpp, значит ключу
          # достаточно версии апстрима.
          key: ccache-eden-v0.2.1-${{ inputs.build_type || 'debug' }}
          restore-keys: |
            ccache-eden-v0.2.1-${{ inputs.build_type || 'debug' }}-
            ccache-eden-v0.2.1-

      - name: Set up ccache
        run: |
          sudo apt-get install -y -qq ccache > /dev/null

          # Pinned, not defaulted - see BUG 1 above.
          echo "CCACHE_DIR=$HOME/.cache/ccache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          export CCACHE_DIR="$HOME/.cache/ccache"
          mkdir -p "$CCACHE_DIR"

          # 3 GB: the full object set for one build type is well under that,
          # and the runner cache limit is 10 GB per repository.
          ccache --set-config=max_size=3G
          # Absolute build paths differ between runs; rewrite them relative to
          # the workspace so the same source hashes the same way.
          ccache --set-config=base_dir="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          ccache --set-config=hash_dir=false
          # The NDK clang binary's mtime changes per runner image; hash what
          # the compiler *is*, not when it was written.
          ccache --set-config=compiler_check=content
          # Harmless for correctness, and stops a changed -I ordering from
          # missing on otherwise identical translation units.
          ccache --set-config=namespace=eden-v0.2.1
          ccache --zero-stats

          echo "CMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          ccache --show-config | grep -E "max_size|cache_dir|base_dir|hash_dir|compiler_check"

      # ── The control build ───────────────────────────────────────────
      #
      # Five installs have crashed and every fix so far has found a real bug
      # that turned out not to be THE bug. Guessing again costs another cycle
      # of the user's time, so this switch removes the guesswork: with
      # apply_patch off, the workflow builds untouched upstream v0.2.1 through
      # the exact same toolchain, keystore and packaging as the patched one.
      #
      #   control crashes too  -> the crash is Eden on that device, not us
      #   control runs, ours does not -> it is in the eleven files of patch2
      #
      # One question, one answer, no more speculation.
      - name: Apply patch2
        if: inputs.apply_patch != false
        run: |
          bash fork/tools/apply_patch2.sh --patch fork/patch2 \
            --eden "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/eden" \
            --subset "${{ inputs.patch_subset || 'all' }}"

      - name: Skip the patch - control build of plain upstream
        if: inputs.apply_patch == false
        run: echo "::warning::building UNPATCHED upstream v0.2.1 as a control"

      # Cached: an 85 MB download that is identical every run, and when it
      # half-arrived once the whole build died at unzip with "End-of-central-
      # directory signature not found" - after the runner had already spent
      # four minutes installing the NDK.
      - name: Cache the Kotlin compiler
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: /tmp/kotlinc
          key: kotlinc-2.0.21

      - name: Check the folder logic before building
        if: inputs.apply_patch != false
        run: |
          # Twenty seconds here against twenty-five minutes of compiling. All
          # three tests run against plain Kotlin - no Android, no device.
          set -euo pipefail

          # The published checksum. A truncated download is otherwise only
          # discovered by unzip failing, which is what happened in run #10.
          KC_SHA=0352c0a45bd22f80f6b26e485cd04da8047baa5de54865281fb9f89a4a7bcf2a

          if [ ! -x /tmp/kotlinc/bin/kotlinc ]; then
            ok=0
            for attempt in 1 2 3; do
              curl -fsSL --retry 3 --retry-all-errors -o /tmp/kc.zip \
                https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin/releases/download/v2.0.21/kotlin-compiler-2.0.21.zip || true
              if [ "$(sha256sum /tmp/kc.zip 2>/dev/null | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$KC_SHA" ]; then
                ok=1; break
              fi
              echo "attempt $attempt: bad or missing download, retrying"
              rm -f /tmp/kc.zip
            done
            [ "$ok" = 1 ] || { echo "::error::could not download the Kotlin compiler"; exit 1; }
            rm -rf /tmp/kotlinc
            unzip -qo /tmp/kc.zip -d /tmp
          else
            echo "kotlinc restored from cache"
          fi

          fail=0

          # GameFolders is the side table that replaced the field on Game.
          echo "── GameFoldersTest ──"
          rm -rf /tmp/gfb && mkdir -p /tmp/gfb
          cp fork/patch2/android/utils/GameFolders.kt fork/patch2/tests/GameFoldersTest.kt /tmp/gfb/
          /tmp/kotlinc/bin/kotlinc /tmp/gfb/*.kt -include-runtime -d /tmp/gf.jar 2>&1 |
            grep -vE "^warning: (classpath|language version)" || true
          java -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -jar /tmp/gf.jar || fail=1

          for t in FolderScanTest GroupByFolderTest CardSubtitleTest StatusVerdictTest MyGamesTest; do
            echo "── $t ──"
            /tmp/kotlinc/bin/kotlinc "fork/patch2/tests/$t.kt" -include-runtime -d "/tmp/$t.jar" 2>&1 |
              grep -vE "^warning: (classpath|language version)" || true
            java -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -jar "/tmp/$t.jar" || fail=1
          done

          exit $fail

      - name: Build
        run: |
          cd eden/src/android
          TYPE="${{ inputs.build_type }}"
          TYPE="${TYPE:-debug}"

          # Upstream already reads a property for extra CMake flags:
          #
          #   val extraCMakeArgs =
          #     (project.findProperty("YUZU_ANDROID_ARGS") as String?)?.split(...)
          #
          # so ccache goes in through the front door, with no edit to Eden's
          # build files. Environment variables alone would NOT work - AGP
          # invokes CMake itself and does not forward them into the configure
          # step, which is the trap that makes people think ccache "did
          # nothing".
          CCACHE_FLAGS="-DCMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache"
          # ── mainline, not legacy ────────────────────────────────────
          #
          # Six builds crashed on the device. All six were assembleLegacy.
          # The official "standard" APK - which is the mainline flavour -
          # runs on the same phone, and that is what finally identified the
          # cause: the flavour, not the patch.
          #
          # "legacy" is described upstream as "patches that improve
          # compatibility with older GPUs (e.g. Snapdragon 865) at the cost
          # of performance". It sets -DYUZU_LEGACY=ON, which defines
          # YUZU_LEGACY - a macro that appears NOWHERE else in the source,
          # checked across every .cpp and .h. So the flavour changed the
          # build without any visible switch in the code, and on a Mali-G57
          # the result did not start.
          #
          # mainline is also what upstream marks isDefault = true.
          # ── The flavour is a variable, because I confounded it once ──
          #
          # A-CONTROL (works) was built LEGACY. B-folders (crashes) was built
          # MAINLINE, because I had switched the flavour in between. So the
          # two differ in TWO ways, not one, and "the patch is guilty" does
          # not follow from that comparison at all.
          #
          # Making it an input means the next comparison changes exactly one
          # thing.
          FLAV="${{ inputs.flavour || 'mainline' }}"
          case "$FLAV" in
            legacy) TASK_BASE="Legacy" ;;
            *)      TASK_BASE="Mainline" ;;
          esac
          echo "flavour: $FLAV"

          if [ "$TYPE" = "release" ]; then
            ./gradlew "assemble${TASK_BASE}Release" -PYUZU_ANDROID_ARGS="$CCACHE_FLAGS" \
              --parallel --build-cache --max-workers="$(nproc)"
          else
            ./gradlew "assemble${TASK_BASE}Debug" -PYUZU_ANDROID_ARGS="$CCACHE_FLAGS" \
              --parallel --build-cache --max-workers="$(nproc)"
          fi

      - name: How much the cache saved
        if: always()
        run: |
          # Printed every run so the effect is visible, not assumed. A first
          # run shows 0% and fills the cache; the next should show most of the
          # 1353 objects coming back as hits.
          ccache --show-stats | head -20

      - name: Verify the changes shipped
        if: inputs.apply_patch != false
        env:
          PATCH_SUBSET: ${{ inputs.patch_subset || 'all' }}
        run: |
          APK=$(find eden -name "*-release.apk" -o -name "*-debug.apk" | head -1)
          echo "APK: $APK ($(du -h "$APK" | cut -f1))"
          echo "MD5: $(md5sum "$APK" | cut -d' ' -f1)"

          # Absolute from here on. The old code cd'd to /tmp/x and then kept
          # using the workspace-relative $APK, which broke the moment anything
          # else in this step wanted to open the file.
          APK="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$APK"

          fail=0

          # ── Why this is checked with Python and not `strings` ───────
          #
          # `strings` does not see UTF-8 Cyrillic in this locale and once
          # reported our Russian labels as missing from a perfectly good APK.
          # The dex is searched byte-for-byte instead.
          #
          # Release and debug are checked differently on purpose. R8 renames
          # and inlines: `folderName` is a real method in debug and is gone
          # from release, inlined into its one caller - which looks identical
          # to the code having been dropped. String literals survive both, so
          # release is verified by the strings the feature cannot work
          # without.
          python3 - "$APK" <<'DEXPY' || fail=1
          import sys, zipfile, io, re, os
          apk = sys.argv[1]
          z = zipfile.ZipFile(apk)
          blob = b"".join(z.read(n) for n in z.namelist() if n.endswith(".dex"))
          release = "release" in apk

          # Only assert what this subset was asked to include. A "folders"
          # build has no floating button by design, and demanding one turns a
          # perfectly good APK into a red run - which is exactly what
          # happened on the first subset build.
          subset = os.environ.get("PATCH_SUBSET", "all")
          folders = subset in ("all", "folders", "depth3")
          minimal = subset == "minimal"
          ui = subset == "ui"
          scan = subset in ("all", "folders", "scan", "sort")
          sort = subset in ("all", "folders", "sort")
          button = subset in ("all", "button")

          wanted = []
          if release:
              # Literals, not names: R8 rewrites names but never these.
              wanted.append(("crash logger", "Symbiosis crash report".encode()))
              if minimal or ui:
                  wanted.append(("floating button position key", b"symbiosis_float_x"))
              if folders:
                  wanted.append(("subtitle separator", " \u00b7 ".encode()))
              elif scan:
                  wanted.append(("crash logger only", b"symbiosis-crash.txt"))
              if button:
                  wanted.append(("floating button position key", b"symbiosis_float_x"))
          else:
              wanted.append(("crash logger", b"installCrashLogger"))
              if minimal or ui:
                  wanted.append(("FloatingGameButton", b"FloatingGameButton"))
              if folders:
                  wanted += [
                      ("groupByFolder", b"groupByFolder"),
                      ("folderName", b"folderName"),
                      ("subtitle separator", " \u00b7 ".encode()),
                  ]
              elif sort:
                  wanted.append(("groupByFolder", b"groupByFolder"))
              elif scan:
                  wanted.append(("folderName", b"folderName"))
              if button:
                  wanted.append(("FloatingGameButton", b"FloatingGameButton"))

          bad = 0
          for label, needle in wanted:
              if needle in blob:
                  print(f"  ok   {label}")
              else:
                  print(f"  MISSING {label}")
                  bad = 1
          sys.exit(bad)
          DEXPY

          python3 - "$APK" <<'SIZEPY' | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import sys, zipfile, os
          apk = sys.argv[1]
          z = zipfile.ZipFile(apk)
          mb = lambda b: b / 1048576
          total = os.path.getsize(apk)
          dex = sum(i.compress_size for i in z.infolist() if i.filename.endswith('.dex'))
          so = sum(i.compress_size for i in z.infolist() if i.filename.endswith('.so'))
          print("## APK")
          print()
          print("| | |")
          print("|---|---|")
          print(f"| size | **{mb(total):.1f} MB** |")
          print(f"| dex | {mb(dex):.1f} MB packed |")
          print(f"| native | {mb(so):.1f} MB packed |")
          SIZEPY

          exit $fail

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: Eden-clean-patch2
          path: eden/src/android/app/build/outputs/apk/**/*.apk
          retention-days: 30


      - name: Upload to gofile.io
        if: github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' || inputs.upload_to_gofile
        run: |
          APK=$(find eden -name "*-release.apk" -o -name "*-debug.apk" | head -1)
          SRV=$(curl -s https://api.gofile.io/servers |
            python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['servers'][0]['name'])")
          curl -s -F "file=@$APK" "https://$SRV.gofile.io/contents/uploadfile" -o /tmp/up.json
          python3 - <<'PY' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import json
          d = json.load(open('/tmp/up.json'))['data']
          print(f"\n- **Download:** {d['downloadPage']}")
          print(f"- **MD5:** `{d['md5']}`")
          print(f"- **Size:** {round(d['size']/1048576,1)} MB")
          PY
          cat "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Run host tests
        # These gate the build deliberately: each was written after a bug
        # reached the user, and each fails against the code that shipped it.
        run: |
          # Ubuntu 24.04 packages fmt 9, but Eden's logging.h calls
          # format.get(), added in fmt 10. Build against the version Eden
          # expects rather than the distribution one.
          git clone --depth 1 --branch 10.2.1 https://github.com/fmtlib/fmt.git /tmp/fmt
          export FMT_INCLUDE=/tmp/fmt/include
          curl -sL -o /tmp/kc.zip https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin/releases/download/v2.0.21/kotlin-compiler-2.0.21.zip
          unzip -q /tmp/kc.zip -d /tmp
          export PATH="/tmp/kotlinc/bin:$PATH"
          bash fork/tools/run_tests.sh --eden "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/eden" --max-skip 3

      - name: Check the Russian localisation
        run: |
          cd eden/src/android/app/src/main/res
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET, re, sys
          def load(p):
              return {e.get('name'): ''.join(e.itertext())
                      for e in ET.parse(p).getroot().iter('string')}
          en, ru = load('values/strings.xml'), load('values-ru/strings.xml')
          fmt = lambda s: sorted(re.findall(r'%(\d+\$[sd]|[sd%])', s))
          bad = [k for k in ru if k in en and fmt(en[k]) != fmt(ru[k])]
          if bad:
              print('format-argument mismatch:', bad[:5]); sys.exit(1)
          print(f'EN {len(en)} / RU {len(ru)} strings, format arguments agree')
          PY

      - name: Build
        run: |
          cd eden/src/android
          # No --no-daemon: the daemon is what lets Gradle keep the Kotlin
          # compiler warm, and the runner has the memory for it. Also ask
          # CMake for every core - the native compile is the long pole and
          # was previously limited to one worker.
          # Release is what the 25 MB budget refers to. Measured on the debug
          # APK: classes.dex and classes15.dex are 22 MB and are STORED
          # UNCOMPRESSED - the same bytes deflate to 9.2 MB, and R8 removes a
          # good deal more before that. Debug stays the default because it
          # keeps the symbols that make a crash report readable.
          TYPE="${{ inputs.build_type }}"
          TYPE="${TYPE:-debug}"
          # Апстрим уже читает YUZU_ANDROID_ARGS для доп. флагов CMake, так
          # что ccache подключается без правки его build-файлов. Переменные
          # окружения тут НЕ работают: AGP сам вызывает CMake и не передаёт
          # их в этап конфигурации.
          CCACHE_FLAGS="-DCMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache"
          if [ "$TYPE" = "release" ]; then
            ./gradlew assembleLegacyRelease -PYUZU_ANDROID_ARGS="$CCACHE_FLAGS" \
              --parallel --build-cache --max-workers="$(nproc)"
          else
            ./gradlew assembleLegacyDebug -PYUZU_ANDROID_ARGS="$CCACHE_FLAGS" \
              --parallel --build-cache --max-workers="$(nproc)"
          fi

      - name: How much the cache saved
        if: always()
        run: ccache --show-stats | head -12

      - name: Verify the fixes actually shipped
        # objdump and dex strings, not a green tick: a build can succeed with
        # a Kotlin file that was never copied into place.
        run: |
          APK=$(find eden -name "*legacy-release.apk" -o -name "*legacy-debug.apk" | head -1)
          echo "APK: $APK ($(du -h "$APK" | cut -f1))"
          echo "MD5: $(md5sum "$APK" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
          mkdir -p /tmp/x && cd /tmp/x && unzip -qo "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$APK" 'classes*.dex' 'lib/*/*.so' 2>/dev/null || \
            unzip -qo "$APK" 'classes*.dex' 'lib/*/*.so'
          fail=0

          # R8 renames Kotlin methods in a release build, so looking for
          # restoreGameDirs there proves nothing and would fail a perfectly
          # good APK. Native symbols survive either way - they are the JNI
          # contract and cannot be renamed - so those are checked always, and
          # the Kotlin names only when they are meant to be present.
          case "$APK" in
            *release*) MINIFIED=1 ;;
            *)         MINIFIED=0 ;;
          esac

          if [ "$MINIFIED" = 0 ]; then
            for sym in restoreGameDirs rememberGameDirs hasActionableButton; do
              if strings classes*.dex | grep -q "$sym"; then echo "  ok   $sym in dex"
              else echo "  MISSING $sym"; fail=1; fi
            done
          else
            echo "  (release build: Kotlin names are minified, skipping that check)"
          fi

          NM=$(find "$ANDROID_HOME/ndk" -name llvm-nm | head -1)
          n=$("$NM" -D lib/arm64-v8a/libyuzu-android.so | grep -c NativeSymbiosis || true)
          echo "  JNI symbols exported: $n"
          [ "$n" -ge 50 ] || { echo "  too few JNI symbols"; fail=1; }

          # The Kenji bridge, in both names. The core dlopen()s libkenjinxjni
          # and calls debug_break from inside deviceInitialize, so a missing
          # copy is a crash on the first device call rather than a warning.
          for lib in libsymbiosis_kenji.so libkenjinxjni.so; do
            if [ -f "lib/arm64-v8a/$lib" ]; then echo "  ok   $lib present"
            else echo "  MISSING $lib"; fail=1; fi
          done
          for sym in debug_break setRenderingThread setCurrentTransform; do
            if "$NM" -D lib/arm64-v8a/libkenjinxjni.so | grep -q " $sym$"; then
              echo "  ok   $sym exported for the core"
            else echo "  MISSING $sym in libkenjinxjni.so"; fail=1; fi
          done

          # What the 25 MB budget is actually about.
          python3 - "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$APK" <<'SIZEPY' | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import sys, zipfile, os
          apk = sys.argv[1]
          z = zipfile.ZipFile(apk)
          total = os.path.getsize(apk)
          dex = sum(i.compress_size for i in z.infolist() if i.filename.endswith('.dex'))
          dex_raw = sum(i.file_size for i in z.infolist() if i.filename.endswith('.dex'))
          so = sum(i.compress_size for i in z.infolist() if i.filename.endswith('.so'))
          stored = sum(i.file_size for i in z.infolist() if i.compress_type == 0)
          mb = lambda b: b / 1048576
          print("## APK size")
          print()
          print("| | |")
          print("|---|---|")
          print(f"| APK | **{mb(total):.1f} MB** |")
          print(f"| dex | {mb(dex):.1f} MB packed (from {mb(dex_raw):.1f} MB) |")
          print(f"| native libraries | {mb(so):.1f} MB packed |")
          print(f"| stored uncompressed | {mb(stored):.1f} MB |")
          print()
          print(("Under the 25 MB target." if mb(total) <= 25
                 else f"Over the 25 MB target by {mb(total) - 25:.1f} MB."))
          SIZEPY

          exit $fail

      - name: Upload the APK as an artefact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: Eden-Symbiosis-Legacy-debug
          path: eden/src/android/app/build/outputs/apk/**/*.apk
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Upload to gofile.io
        # Default to uploading. inputs.* is empty for a push-triggered run, so
        # the plain condition silently skipped the step and the summary carried
        # no download link - the APK existed only as an artifact, which needs a
        # signed-in browser and expires. Only an explicit false opts out.
        if: github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' || inputs.upload_to_gofile
        run: |
          APK=$(find eden -name "*legacy-release.apk" -o -name "*legacy-debug.apk" | head -1)
          SRV=$(curl -s https://api.gofile.io/servers | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['servers'][0]['name'])")
          curl -s -F "file=@$APK" "https://$SRV.gofile.io/contents/uploadfile" -o /tmp/up.json
          python3 - <<'PY' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import json
          d = json.load(open('/tmp/up.json'))['data']
          print(f"## APK\n\n- **Download:** {d['downloadPage']}\n- **MD5:** `{d['md5']}`\n- **Size:** {round(d['size']/1048576,1)} MB")
          PY
          cat "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

=== build2.yml ===
name: Build clean

# Builds official Eden with patch2 on top - four modified files, nothing else.
#
# WHY A SECOND WORKFLOW
#   build.yml applies the old Symbiosis tree: 13 extra screens, 376 KB of C++,
#   and the retro launcher whose early return in SetWindowAdaptPass() caused
#   the settings crash. This one starts from clean upstream and adds only what
#   was actually asked for, so anything that breaks here is mine and recent.
#
# WHAT PATCH2 CHANGES
#   Game.kt          a game records the folder it was found in
#   GameHelper.kt    that folder is carried down the scan; depth 3 -> 24
#   GamesFragment.kt the list is ordered by folder, then by title
#   GameAdapter.kt   that folder is shown on the card
#   SharedDataDirectory.kt   the shared-folder utility, unchanged
#
# THE CORE STAYS INSIDE THE APK
#   Splitting it out into a folder was tried and abandoned: it cost four
#   failed installs and never once produced a working build. The core is
#   loaded by Eden's own untouched System.loadLibrary, exactly as upstream
#   does it. patch2 no longer contains NativeLibrary.kt at all - there is
#   nothing left in it to change.
#
#   Nothing is created, moved or written. Folder permissions stay read-only and
#   config.ini is untouched.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      build_type:
        description: "debug keeps symbols; release runs R8"
        type: choice
        options: [debug, release]
        default: debug
      upload_to_gofile:
        description: "Also upload the APK to gofile.io"
        type: boolean
        default: true
      apply_patch:
        description: "off = plain upstream Eden, no patch at all (control build)"
        type: boolean
        default: true
      patch_subset:
        description: "which parts of patch2 to apply: all | folders | button | shared"
        type: choice
        options: [all, ui, status, folders, depth3, scan, sort, button, shared, minimal]
        default: all
      flavour:
        description: "mainline (upstream default) or legacy (what the working control was built with)"
        type: choice
        options: [mainline, legacy]
        default: mainline
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'patch2/**'
      - 'tools/apply_patch2.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/build2.yml'

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90

    steps:
      - name: Check out this fork
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          path: fork

      - name: Check out upstream Eden
        run: |
          # Retried, with our mirror behind it: git.eden-emu.dev answered 502
          # mid-build once and took the whole run down with it.
          ok=0
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if git clone --branch v0.2.1 \
                 https://git.eden-emu.dev/eden-emu/eden.git eden 2>/tmp/clone.log; then
              ok=1; break
            fi
            echo "attempt $attempt failed:"; tail -3 /tmp/clone.log
            rm -rf eden
            sleep $((attempt * 10))
          done
          if [ "$ok" != 1 ]; then
            # The mirror, AT THE TAG. This fallback used to clone the mirror's
            # default branch, which is a different commit entirely - so when
            # upstream answered 502 the build silently switched to other code
            # and died in CMake with an error that looked like ours. Twice.
            echo "::warning::upstream unreachable; using our mirror at v0.2.1"
            git clone --branch v0.2.1 \
              https://github.com/sj0404-collab/eden-upstream-reference.git eden \
              || { echo "::error::neither upstream nor the mirror could be cloned"; exit 1; }
          fi

          cd eden
          rev=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
          echo "upstream: $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"

          # Whichever source answered, it must be the tag we build against.
          # Anything else is a different emulator wearing the same directory
          # name, and the failure surfaces 20 minutes later as a C++ error.
          expected=58c1e20ee58efa3900ba616207d460886214480b
          if [ "$rev" != "$expected" ]; then
            echo "::error::wrong upstream commit: $rev (expected v0.2.1 = $expected)"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "  ok   upstream is v0.2.1"

      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - uses: android-actions/setup-android@v3

      - name: Install NDK, CMake and glslang
        run: |
          sdkmanager --install "ndk;28.2.13676358" "cmake;3.31.6" \
            "build-tools;35.0.0" "platforms;android-36" > /dev/null
          sudo apt-get update -qq
          sudo apt-get install -y -qq glslang-tools > /dev/null

      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.gradle/caches
            ~/.gradle/wrapper
          key: gradle2-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('eden/src/android/**/*.gradle*') }}
          restore-keys: gradle2-${{ runner.os }}-

      # ── Why the build took twenty-five minutes ──────────────────────
      #
      # Measured from a real run's timestamps:
      #     12:49:41  Kotlin compiled
      #     12:51:38  ninja started
      #     13:11:56  APK ready          <- twenty minutes of C++
      #
      # 1353 C++ objects were rebuilt from scratch. patch2 contains nine .kt
      # files and three .xml files and NOT ONE .cpp - so every second of that
      # was spent recompiling code nobody touched.
      #
      # ccache fixes exactly this: identical source plus identical flags means
      # the object file is copied out of the cache instead of compiled. The
      # first run after this fills the cache and is no faster; every run after
      # that skips the part that dominates the clock.
      # ── Two bugs in the first attempt at this, both proved by run #9 ──
      #
      # BUG 1: THE CACHE WAS SAVED SOMEWHERE ELSE THAN IT WAS READ
      #   The path here said ~/.ccache. ccache itself reported
      #       (default) cache_dir = /home/runner/.cache/ccache
      #   so 1678 freshly compiled objects were written to a directory the
      #   cache action never packed. Nothing was wrong with ccache and nothing
      #   was wrong with the key - the two halves simply pointed at different
      #   folders. CCACHE_DIR is now set explicitly and the path below is the
      #   same variable, so they cannot drift apart again.
      #
      # BUG 2: HASHED PATHS DEFEAT THE CACHE ACROSS RUNS
      #   NDK builds bake absolute paths into the object; ccache's default
      #   direct mode hashes the compiler binary's mtime too. On a fresh
      #   runner that is a different value every time, which is why run #9
      #   showed 0.89% hits even for the objects it had just built - the 15
      #   hits it did get were all "preprocessed", never "direct".
      #   base_dir + hash_dir=false + compiler_check=content fix exactly that.
      - name: Cache the C++ objects
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          # Must match CCACHE_DIR below. It did not, and that alone cost the
          # entire 20 minutes this step exists to save.
          path: ~/.cache/ccache
          # Keyed on the upstream tag, not on our patch: our patch never
          # changes a .cpp, so a new key would throw away a cache that is
          # still perfectly valid.
          # Не github.run_number: он новый на каждом запуске, поэтому
          # прямого попадания не бывает никогда - только запасной поиск по
          # префиксу, а он не срабатывает, если прошлая сборка упала до
          # шага сохранения. patch2 не трогает ни одного .cpp, значит ключу
          # достаточно версии апстрима.
          key: ccache-eden-v0.2.1-${{ inputs.build_type || 'debug' }}
          restore-keys: |
            ccache-eden-v0.2.1-${{ inputs.build_type || 'debug' }}-
            ccache-eden-v0.2.1-

      - name: Set up ccache
        run: |
          sudo apt-get install -y -qq ccache > /dev/null

          # Pinned, not defaulted - see BUG 1 above.
          echo "CCACHE_DIR=$HOME/.cache/ccache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          export CCACHE_DIR="$HOME/.cache/ccache"
          mkdir -p "$CCACHE_DIR"

          # 3 GB: the full object set for one build type is well under that,
          # and the runner cache limit is 10 GB per repository.
          ccache --set-config=max_size=3G
          # Absolute build paths differ between runs; rewrite them relative to
          # the workspace so the same source hashes the same way.
          ccache --set-config=base_dir="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          ccache --set-config=hash_dir=false
          # The NDK clang binary's mtime changes per runner image; hash what
          # the compiler *is*, not when it was written.
          ccache --set-config=compiler_check=content
          # Harmless for correctness, and stops a changed -I ordering from
          # missing on otherwise identical translation units.
          ccache --set-config=namespace=eden-v0.2.1
          ccache --zero-stats

          echo "CMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          ccache --show-config | grep -E "max_size|cache_dir|base_dir|hash_dir|compiler_check"

      # ── The control build ───────────────────────────────────────────
      #
      # Five installs have crashed and every fix so far has found a real bug
      # that turned out not to be THE bug. Guessing again costs another cycle
      # of the user's time, so this switch removes the guesswork: with
      # apply_patch off, the workflow builds untouched upstream v0.2.1 through
      # the exact same toolchain, keystore and packaging as the patched one.
      #
      #   control crashes too  -> the crash is Eden on that device, not us
      #   control runs, ours does not -> it is in the eleven files of patch2
      #
      # One question, one answer, no more speculation.
      - name: Apply patch2
        if: inputs.apply_patch != false
        run: |
          bash fork/tools/apply_patch2.sh --patch fork/patch2 \
            --eden "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/eden" \
            --subset "${{ inputs.patch_subset || 'all' }}"

      - name: Skip the patch - control build of plain upstream
        if: inputs.apply_patch == false
        run: echo "::warning::building UNPATCHED upstream v0.2.1 as a control"

      # Cached: an 85 MB download that is identical every run, and when it
      # half-arrived once the whole build died at unzip with "End-of-central-
      # directory signature not found" - after the runner had already spent
      # four minutes installing the NDK.
      - name: Cache the Kotlin compiler
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: /tmp/kotlinc
          key: kotlinc-2.0.21

      - name: Check the folder logic before building
        if: inputs.apply_patch != false
        run: |
          # Twenty seconds here against twenty-five minutes of compiling. All
          # three tests run against plain Kotlin - no Android, no device.
          set -euo pipefail

          # The published checksum. A truncated download is otherwise only
          # discovered by unzip failing, which is what happened in run #10.
          KC_SHA=0352c0a45bd22f80f6b26e485cd04da8047baa5de54865281fb9f89a4a7bcf2a

          if [ ! -x /tmp/kotlinc/bin/kotlinc ]; then
            ok=0
            for attempt in 1 2 3; do
              curl -fsSL --retry 3 --retry-all-errors -o /tmp/kc.zip \
                https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin/releases/download/v2.0.21/kotlin-compiler-2.0.21.zip || true
              if [ "$(sha256sum /tmp/kc.zip 2>/dev/null | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$KC_SHA" ]; then
                ok=1; break
              fi
              echo "attempt $attempt: bad or missing download, retrying"
              rm -f /tmp/kc.zip
            done
            [ "$ok" = 1 ] || { echo "::error::could not download the Kotlin compiler"; exit 1; }
            rm -rf /tmp/kotlinc
            unzip -qo /tmp/kc.zip -d /tmp
          else
            echo "kotlinc restored from cache"
          fi

          fail=0

          # GameFolders is the side table that replaced the field on Game.
          echo "── GameFoldersTest ──"
          rm -rf /tmp/gfb && mkdir -p /tmp/gfb
          cp fork/patch2/android/utils/GameFolders.kt fork/patch2/tests/GameFoldersTest.kt /tmp/gfb/
          /tmp/kotlinc/bin/kotlinc /tmp/gfb/*.kt -include-runtime -d /tmp/gf.jar 2>&1 |
            grep -vE "^warning: (classpath|language version)" || true
          java -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -jar /tmp/gf.jar || fail=1

          for t in FolderScanTest GroupByFolderTest CardSubtitleTest StatusVerdictTest MyGamesTest; do
            echo "── $t ──"
            /tmp/kotlinc/bin/kotlinc "fork/patch2/tests/$t.kt" -include-runtime -d "/tmp/$t.jar" 2>&1 |
              grep -vE "^warning: (classpath|language version)" || true
            java -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -jar "/tmp/$t.jar" || fail=1
          done

          exit $fail

      - name: Build
        run: |
          cd eden/src/android
          TYPE="${{ inputs.build_type }}"
          TYPE="${TYPE:-debug}"

          # Upstream already reads a property for extra CMake flags:
          #
          #   val extraCMakeArgs =
          #     (project.findProperty("YUZU_ANDROID_ARGS") as String?)?.split(...)
          #
          # so ccache goes in through the front door, with no edit to Eden's
          # build files. Environment variables alone would NOT work - AGP
          # invokes CMake itself and does not forward them into the configure
          # step, which is the trap that makes people think ccache "did
          # nothing".
          CCACHE_FLAGS="-DCMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache"
          # ── mainline, not legacy ────────────────────────────────────
          #
          # Six builds crashed on the device. All six were assembleLegacy.
          # The official "standard" APK - which is the mainline flavour -
          # runs on the same phone, and that is what finally identified the
          # cause: the flavour, not the patch.
          #
          # "legacy" is described upstream as "patches that improve
          # compatibility with older GPUs (e.g. Snapdragon 865) at the cost
          # of performance". It sets -DYUZU_LEGACY=ON, which defines
          # YUZU_LEGACY - a macro that appears NOWHERE else in the source,
          # checked across every .cpp and .h. So the flavour changed the
          # build without any visible switch in the code, and on a Mali-G57
          # the result did not start.
          #
          # mainline is also what upstream marks isDefault = true.
          # ── The flavour is a variable, because I confounded it once ──
          #
          # A-CONTROL (works) was built LEGACY. B-folders (crashes) was built
          # MAINLINE, because I had switched the flavour in between. So the
          # two differ in TWO ways, not one, and "the patch is guilty" does
          # not follow from that comparison at all.
          #
          # Making it an input means the next comparison changes exactly one
          # thing.
          FLAV="${{ inputs.flavour || 'mainline' }}"
          case "$FLAV" in
            legacy) TASK_BASE="Legacy" ;;
            *)      TASK_BASE="Mainline" ;;
          esac
          echo "flavour: $FLAV"

          if [ "$TYPE" = "release" ]; then
            ./gradlew "assemble${TASK_BASE}Release" -PYUZU_ANDROID_ARGS="$CCACHE_FLAGS" \
              --parallel --build-cache --max-workers="$(nproc)"
          else
            ./gradlew "assemble${TASK_BASE}Debug" -PYUZU_ANDROID_ARGS="$CCACHE_FLAGS" \
              --parallel --build-cache --max-workers="$(nproc)"
          fi

      - name: How much the cache saved
        if: always()
        run: |
          # Printed every run so the effect is visible, not assumed. A first
          # run shows 0% and fills the cache; the next should show most of the
          # 1353 objects coming back as hits.
          ccache --show-stats | head -20

      - name: Verify the changes shipped
        if: inputs.apply_patch != false
        env:
          PATCH_SUBSET: ${{ inputs.patch_subset || 'all' }}
        run: |
          APK=$(find eden -name "*-release.apk" -o -name "*-debug.apk" | head -1)
          echo "APK: $APK ($(du -h "$APK" | cut -f1))"
          echo "MD5: $(md5sum "$APK" | cut -d' ' -f1)"

          # Absolute from here on. The old code cd'd to /tmp/x and then kept
          # using the workspace-relative $APK, which broke the moment anything
          # else in this step wanted to open the file.
          APK="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$APK"

          fail=0

          # ── Why this is checked with Python and not `strings` ───────
          #
          # `strings` does not see UTF-8 Cyrillic in this locale and once
          # reported our Russian labels as missing from a perfectly good APK.
          # The dex is searched byte-for-byte instead.
          #
          # Release and debug are checked differently on purpose. R8 renames
          # and inlines: `folderName` is a real method in debug and is gone
          # from release, inlined into its one caller - which looks identical
          # to the code having been dropped. String literals survive both, so
          # release is verified by the strings the feature cannot work
          # without.
          python3 - "$APK" <<'DEXPY' || fail=1
          import sys, zipfile, io, re, os
          apk = sys.argv[1]
          z = zipfile.ZipFile(apk)
          blob = b"".join(z.read(n) for n in z.namelist() if n.endswith(".dex"))
          release = "release" in apk

          # Only assert what this subset was asked to include. A "folders"
          # build has no floating button by design, and demanding one turns a
          # perfectly good APK into a red run - which is exactly what
          # happened on the first subset build.
          subset = os.environ.get("PATCH_SUBSET", "all")
          folders = subset in ("all", "folders", "depth3")
          minimal = subset == "minimal"
          ui = subset == "ui"
          scan = subset in ("all", "folders", "scan", "sort")
          sort = subset in ("all", "folders", "sort")
          button = subset in ("all", "button")

          wanted = []
          if release:
              # Literals, not names: R8 rewrites names but never these.
              wanted.append(("crash logger", "Symbiosis crash report".encode()))
              if minimal or ui:
                  wanted.append(("floating button position key", b"symbiosis_float_x"))
              if folders:
                  wanted.append(("subtitle separator", " \u00b7 ".encode()))
              elif scan:
                  wanted.append(("crash logger only", b"symbiosis-crash.txt"))
              if button:
                  wanted.append(("floating button position key", b"symbiosis_float_x"))
          else:
              wanted.append(("crash logger", b"installCrashLogger"))
              if minimal or ui:
                  wanted.append(("FloatingGameButton", b"FloatingGameButton"))
              if folders:
                  wanted += [
                      ("groupByFolder", b"groupByFolder"),
                      ("folderName", b"folderName"),
                      ("subtitle separator", " \u00b7 ".encode()),
                  ]
              elif sort:
                  wanted.append(("groupByFolder", b"groupByFolder"))
              elif scan:
                  wanted.append(("folderName", b"folderName"))
              if button:
                  wanted.append(("FloatingGameButton", b"FloatingGameButton"))

          bad = 0
          for label, needle in wanted:
              if needle in blob:
                  print(f"  ok   {label}")
              else:
                  print(f"  MISSING {label}")
                  bad = 1
          sys.exit(bad)
          DEXPY

          python3 - "$APK" <<'SIZEPY' | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import sys, zipfile, os
          apk = sys.argv[1]
          z = zipfile.ZipFile(apk)
          mb = lambda b: b / 1048576
          total = os.path.getsize(apk)
          dex = sum(i.compress_size for i in z.infolist() if i.filename.endswith('.dex'))
          so = sum(i.compress_size for i in z.infolist() if i.filename.endswith('.so'))
          print("## APK")
          print()
          print("| | |")
          print("|---|---|")
          print(f"| size | **{mb(total):.1f} MB** |")
          print(f"| dex | {mb(dex):.1f} MB packed |")
          print(f"| native | {mb(so):.1f} MB packed |")
          SIZEPY

          exit $fail

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: Eden-clean-patch2
          path: eden/src/android/app/build/outputs/apk/**/*.apk
          retention-days: 30


      - name: Upload to gofile.io
        if: github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' || inputs.upload_to_gofile
        run: |
          APK=$(find eden -name "*-release.apk" -o -name "*-debug.apk" | head -1)
          SRV=$(curl -s https://api.gofile.io/servers |
            python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['servers'][0]['name'])")
          curl -s -F "file=@$APK" "https://$SRV.gofile.io/contents/uploadfile" -o /tmp/up.json
          python3 - <<'PY' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import json
          d = json.load(open('/tmp/up.json'))['data']
          print(f"\n- **Download:** {d['downloadPage']}")
          print(f"- **MD5:** `{d['md5']}`")
          print(f"- **Size:** {round(d['size']/1048576,1)} MB")
          PY
          cat "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

Now I understand the project. Two build workflows:
- build.yml: applies `patch/` (full Symbiosis tree, with retro launcher, 13 screens, C++)
- build2.yml: applies `patch2/` (5-11 files, clean)

The user's bug: "одну игру видит а остальные не видит... лаунчер не прокручивается влево вправо".

build2.yml's description says patch2 changes GamesFragment: "the list is ordered by folder, then by title". And patch2 has `card_game_grid.xml`, `card_game_carousel.xml` etc.

Which one is the "launcher"? In patch/ there's the retro launcher (card_launcher.xml, LauncherAdapter.kt, bg_launcher_swatch.xml). The user said "лаунчер не прокручивается влево вправо" — the launcher doesn't scroll left-right. A carousel scrolls left/right.

Hmm, but the user also said "одну игру видит а остальные не видит а раз не видит то и не открывает" — sees one game, doesn't see the rest, and because it doesn't see them it doesn't open them.

This sounds like the Games screen (games list / carousel) where only one game card is displayed. Possibly in landscape `layout-land/fragment_games.xml` there's a ViewPager2 carousel that shows one item and doesn't scroll.

Let me look at the actual layouts and fragments. Let me read patch/android/layout-land/fragment_games.xml and card_game_carousel.xml and the GamesFragment.

Let me also check docs/BUGS.md — that likely documents known bugs, and might mention this one. And README for context.

Let me read in parallel: card_game_carousel.xml, layout-land/fragment_games.xml (382 lines), and grep for ViewPager in the patch.

Actually let me be smart about context. Let me delegate exploration to a subagent? The user wants a fix. I should understand the actual bug well. Let me first grep for ViewPager2 / carousel to locate the horizontal scroll.

Critical Android WebView consideration: **`body { overflow:hidden; display:flex; flex-direction:column; }` and the whole page is a fixed layout.** In a WebView, touch-scrolling an inner `overflow-x:auto` div works normally... unless the WebView is configured with an overriding OnTouchListener that consumes events, or `setOverScrollMode`, or the WebView is inside a ViewPager2.

Hmm! That's a strong lead: if the library.html is hosted in a WebView inside a ViewPager2 (or a horizontal swipe container), the parent's horizontal drag steals the touch from the rail. Let me check LivePanel.kt — how the WebView is set up.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Builds and runs the host test suite against a patched Eden checkout.
#
# Two things here are easy to get wrong and both make the suite worthless:
#
#  1. Do NOT put <eden>/src/common on the include path. Eden ships its own
#     common/assert.h, which shadows the standard <cassert>; every assert()
#     then expands to nothing and the tests pass without checking anything.
#     Only -I<eden>/src is correct.
#
#  2. Eden's logging is a real dependency of the layer. Rather than linking
#     half the emulator, a tiny stub supplies FmtLogMessageImpl.
#
# Usage: bash tools/run_tests.sh [--eden <dir>]
set -uo pipefail

EDEN_DIR="${EDEN_DIR:-/tmp/citest}"
# A test that will not link proves nothing. Allow a known few (they need most
# of video_core), but fail if the number grows - that means the environment is
# broken, not the code.
MAX_SKIP="${MAX_SKIP:-99}"
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --max-skip) MAX_SKIP="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --eden) EDEN_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    *) echo "unknown argument: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

E="$EDEN_DIR"
S="$E/src/common/symbiosis"
[ -d "$S" ] || { echo "patched Eden not found at $E (run tools/apply_patch.sh first)" >&2; exit 1; }

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

# Eden's logging.h needs fmt 10 (format.get()); Ubuntu ships fmt 9. Point
# FMT_INCLUDE at a fmt 10 checkout to build against that instead. FMT_HEADER_ONLY
# avoids needing the compiled library at all.
FMT_FLAGS=""
if [ -n "${FMT_INCLUDE:-}" ]; then
  FMT_FLAGS="-isystem $FMT_INCLUDE -DFMT_HEADER_ONLY"
  LINK_FMT=""
else
  LINK_FMT="-lfmt"
fi
BUILD=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$BUILD"' EXIT

# Minimal stand-in for Eden's logging backend.
cat > "$BUILD/log_stub.cpp" <<'STUB'

And it's worse than they thought: the empty message lies ("нет игр — откройте Список и добавьте папку") when the library actually has 8 games. This is a confirmed, reproduced bug. Root cause: `renderLauncher()` → `RAIL_LIST = visibleGames()`, and `visibleGames()` applies the Список tab's search text and filter. Secondary defects confirmed: - No position indicator anywhere (`railHasCounter: False`), and the scrollbar is hidden → with 1.5 slides visible there is no cue that more games exist. - The search input re-renders only `render()` (line 1599), not `renderLauncher()` → the launcher keeps a stale list until the next loadGames(); so the rail and the dock can disagree with the list. Split the shared sort out of `visibleGames()`: ```js function sortGames(list) { return list.sort((a,b) => { ... }); } function visibleGames() { // вкладка «Список»: поиск и фильтр применяются здесь ... filter ... return sortGames(list); } function railGames() { // вкладка «Лаунчер»: вся библиотека return sortGames(GAMES.slice()); } ``` 2. `renderLauncher()` uses `RAIL_LIST = railGames();` 3. `render()` should also refresh the rail so the two tabs can't disagree — careful: `render()` is called on every keystroke of the search box. Re-rendering the rail on each keystroke would rebuild 8+ slides and reset covers — wasteful and would fight the user's position in the carousel. Better: keep them decoupled, which is precisely the point — the rail doesn't depend on the list filter at all. So no need to call renderLauncher from render(). But there IS a real ordering bug: if GAMES changes, both need updating — `loadGames()` already calls both. Good. However: with the rail no longer filtered, if `GAMES` is empty the message stays. Fine. 4. Keep LAUNCH_I pointing at the same game when possible. When the list changes (loadGames), LAUNCH_I is an index into a differently-ordered/filtered list. Minor: not required for this fix. But there is a related real annoyance: after `loadGames()` the rail resets to index 0? No — LAUNCH_I is preserved as an index, clamped. With the fix, indices are stable because the rail list no longer changes with filters. Good — the fix also makes the index stable. 5.
